Pulse channels (BLE / WiFi / cellular / IR) draw the scan-event timestamps and signal levels reported by the Android system, held sample-and-hold into square waves; this is not a physical capture of the over-the-air RF waveform and does not represent occupied bandwidth. The cellular channel is discrete samples polled every 2s; the IR channel only gets a trace after a real transmit pattern is injected via submitIrPattern.

Amplitude mapping: BLE / WiFi = (RSSI + 100) / 80 (-100 dBm → 0%, -20 dBm → 100%); cellular = (RSRP + 140) / 100 (-140 → 0%, -40 → 100%); audio = (dBFS + 80) / 80 (-80 dBFS → 0%, 0 dBFS → 100%); IR carrier = 100%, gap = 0%.

The audio channel uses AudioRecord 16kHz / 16bit / mono with an 8kHz bandwidth cap; every 100ms, 1600 raw samples are compressed into one RMS envelope point (10Hz), drawing an energy envelope rather than the raw audio waveform; 16kHz sampling cannot reproduce detail above 8kHz.

Samples beyond a channel\'s range are clamped to the 0% / 100% edges in the plot, and readouts are labelled with the ≤ / ≥ range endpoint instead of faking an exact number; the dBFS value in the audio tag is the real measurement for that frame.

All readouts come from real system API return values; with no data the UI shows \"--\" and never interpolates or fabricates. Colors only distinguish channels; this page is an engineering debug visualization, not a spectrum analyzer, and has no direction-finding or positioning capability.

Permissions: BLE scan, Wi-Fi scan / location, phone state and recording are requested centrally by the app gateway; when a permission is missing the affected channel shows the exact reason instead of failing silently.
